findings.text: the process-wide cache re-implements the memo the repository already owns: reckon/file_memo.py:445 memoized_key is documented as the memo for a derivation whose caller carries its complete change key, which is exactly the (project, root, store path, store stamp) key this dict builds, so a second memo now exists for one capability; it is non-blocking because the local dict deliberately replaces its entry rather than accruing one per stamp and hands out the stored rows instead of the copies file_memo makes.

the cache hands every caller the same list object and the same row dicts, and the docstring's claim that every caller reads history is asserted rather than enforced, so one consumer that mutated a row would corrupt the answer for the whole process until the store's token next moved; non-blocking because today's callers at reckon/roadmap.py:3798 and reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py:977 only read through _collect, which builds new dicts.

this assertion compares the read's answer against the run id the test itself handed run_store.append one line earlier, so it proves the store round-trips the test's own value rather than deriving its expectation from an independent read of the store; the stale-cache guard in this test is carried by the decode count at line 212, not by this line.
